scenes.headline: 10 companies that went public fastest
scenes.body: And what happened to them next.
scenes.voiceover: Most companies take ten years or more to reach the stock market. These ten did it in months. But speed didn't always mean success.

scenes.headline: IPO: the first time a company sells shares to the public
scenes.body: An initial public offering, on a stock exchange.
scenes.voiceover: First, a quick definition. An I P O, or initial public offering, is the first time a company sells its shares to the public on a stock exchange.

scenes.headline: From legal registration to its first day of trading
scenes.body: Traditional IPOs on major exchanges only. No SPACs or over-the-counter listings. The fastest we could verify, as of November 2026.
scenes.voiceover: Here's how we counted: from the day each company was legally registered to its first day of trading on a major stock exchange. These are the fastest we could verify, and every one has its source on screen.

scenes.headline: PDD (Pinduoduo)
scenes.voiceover: Number ten.

scenes.name: PDD (Pinduoduo)
scenes.headline: China · E-commerce
scenes.receipt: Founded 2015 → Nasdaq IPO 26 Jul 2018 · DealStreetAsia; Global Venturing
scenes.voiceover: P D D, better known as Pinduoduo, from China. It's an online shopping platform built on group buying, and today it owns Temu. Founded in twenty fifteen, it listed on Nasdaq in July twenty eighteen, raising one point six billion dollars, about three years after it started.

scenes.name: PDD (Pinduoduo)
scenes.headline: Still listed, and now the owner of Temu
scenes.receipt: DealStreetAsia; Global Venturing
scenes.voiceover: Unlike some on this list, it's still very much alive.

scenes.headline: Qutoutiao
scenes.voiceover: Number nine.

scenes.name: Qutoutiao
scenes.headline: China · Mobile news app

stat.label: Registered Jun 2016 → first trading day 14 Sep 2018

scenes.receipt: Founded Jun 2016 → Nasdaq IPO 14 Sep 2018 · Caixin; Renaissance Capital
scenes.voiceover: Qutoutiao, a Chinese news app whose name means fun headlines. Founded in June twenty sixteen, it listed on Nasdaq in September twenty eighteen, about twenty-seven months later, and its shares more than doubled on day one.

scenes.name: Qutoutiao
scenes.headline: Agreed to leave Nasdaq in 2023
scenes.receipt: Caixin; Renaissance Capital
scenes.voiceover: But the early excitement didn't last. In twenty twenty-three, it agreed to leave Nasdaq.

scenes.headline: Luckin Coffee
scenes.voiceover: Number eight.

scenes.name: Luckin Coffee
scenes.headline: China · Coffee chain

stat.label: Registered Jun 2017 → first trading day 17 May 2019

scenes.receipt: Cayman holding co. registered Jun 2017 → Nasdaq IPO 17 May 2019 · Luckin SEC filings; TechCrunch
scenes.voiceover: Luckin Coffee, a Chinese coffee chain built for app ordering and pickup. Its holding company was registered in June twenty seventeen, and it listed on Nasdaq in May twenty nineteen, raising about six hundred and fifty million dollars.

scenes.name: Luckin Coffee
scenes.headline: Fabricated sales, then removed from Nasdaq
scenes.receipt: Luckin SEC filings; TechCrunch
scenes.voiceover: Then, in April twenty twenty, the company itself announced that some of its sales had been fabricated. Trading was halted, and it was removed from Nasdaq. The coffee shops kept running in China, but the listing didn't survive.

scenes.headline: Priceline
scenes.voiceover: Number seven.

scenes.name: Priceline
scenes.headline: USA · Online travel

stat.label: Registered Jul 1997 → first trading day 30 Mar 1999

scenes.receipt: Incorporated 1997* → Nasdaq IPO 30 Mar 1999 · Encyclopedia.com; Benzinga  (*sources differ on 1996–97)
scenes.voiceover: Priceline, the American name-your-own-price travel site. Incorporated in nineteen ninety-seven, it listed in March nineteen ninety-nine. On its first day, it was valued at around ten billion dollars.

scenes.name: Priceline
scenes.headline: Today it's part of Booking Holdings
scenes.receipt: Encyclopedia.com; Benzinga  (*sources differ on 1996–97)
scenes.voiceover: It survived the dot-com crash, and today it's part of Booking Holdings, the company behind Booking dot com.

scenes.headline: Sycamore Networks
scenes.voiceover: Number six.

scenes.name: Sycamore Networks
scenes.headline: USA · Telecom equipment

stat.label: Registered 17 Feb 1998 → first trading day 21 Oct 1999

scenes.receipt: Incorporated 17 Feb 1998 → Nasdaq IPO 21 Oct 1999 · Sycamore SEC 10-K
scenes.voiceover: Sycamore Networks, an American maker of fibre-optic network equipment. Incorporated in February nineteen ninety-eight, it listed twenty months later, in October nineteen ninety-nine, with just a few products and one customer. Its shares almost quintupled on day one.

scenes.name: Sycamore Networks
scenes.headline: Sold its business and dissolved
scenes.receipt: Sycamore SEC 10-K
scenes.voiceover: When the telecom boom ended, so did its growth. In twenty thirteen, it sold its business and dissolved.

scenes.headline: Netscape
scenes.voiceover: Number five.

scenes.name: Netscape
scenes.headline: USA · Web browser

stat.label: Registered 4 Apr 1994 → first trading day 9 Aug 1995

scenes.receipt: Founded 4 Apr 1994 → Nasdaq IPO 9 Aug 1995 · Britannica; Wikipedia
scenes.voiceover: Netscape, the company whose web browser brought the internet to millions. Founded in April nineteen ninety-four, it went public just sixteen months later, in August nineteen ninety-five, without ever having made a profit.

scenes.name: Netscape
scenes.headline: The IPO that started the dot-com rush
scenes.receipt: Britannica; Wikipedia
scenes.voiceover: Its stock doubled on day one, and that moment kicked off the dot-com boom. In nineteen ninety-eight, it was bought by AOL.

scenes.headline: Akamai
scenes.voiceover: Number four.

scenes.name: Akamai
scenes.headline: USA · Internet infrastructure

stat.label: Registered 20 Aug 1998 → first trading day 29 Oct 1999

scenes.receipt: Incorporated 20 Aug 1998 → Nasdaq IPO 29 Oct 1999 · Akamai company history; Encyclopedia.com
scenes.voiceover: Akamai, from the United States. It runs the networks of servers that make websites load faster around the world. Incorporated in August nineteen ninety-eight, it listed about fourteen months later.

scenes.name: Akamai
scenes.headline: Still a major internet company today
scenes.receipt: Akamai company history; Encyclopedia.com
scenes.voiceover: It survived the crash, and it's still a major internet company today.

scenes.headline: Yahoo
scenes.voiceover: Number three.

scenes.name: Yahoo
scenes.headline: USA · Internet portal

stat.label: Registered 2 Mar 1995 → first trading day 12 Apr 1996

scenes.receipt: Incorporated 2 Mar 1995 → Nasdaq IPO 12 Apr 1996 · History of Yahoo (Wikipedia); Entrepreneur
scenes.voiceover: Yahoo. It started as two Stanford students' list of websites, but the company was only registered in March nineteen ninety-five. Just over thirteen months later, in April nineteen ninety-six, it went public.

scenes.name: Yahoo
scenes.headline: Sold to Verizon for about $4.5 billion
scenes.receipt: History of Yahoo (Wikipedia); Entrepreneur
scenes.voiceover: Yahoo became one of the biggest names on the internet. In twenty seventeen, its main business was sold to Verizon for about four and a half billion dollars.

scenes.headline: Pets.com
scenes.voiceover: Number two.

scenes.name: Pets.com
scenes.headline: USA · Online pet supplies

stat.label: Registered Feb 1999 → first trading day Feb 2000

scenes.receipt: Incorporated Feb 1999 → Nasdaq IPO Feb 2000 · Wikipedia (Pets.com S-1); Business Insider
scenes.voiceover: Pets dot com, an American online pet shop famous for its sock-puppet mascot. Incorporated in February nineteen ninety-nine, it listed on Nasdaq exactly a year later.

scenes.name: Pets.com
scenes.headline: Liquidated 268 days after its IPO
scenes.receipt: Wikipedia (Pets.com S-1); Business Insider
scenes.voiceover: It lost money on almost every sale. Two hundred and sixty-eight days after its IPO, it shut down, and its shares, sold at eleven dollars, were worth nineteen cents.

scenes.headline: Lycos
scenes.voiceover: Number one.

scenes.name: Lycos
scenes.headline: USA · Internet search

stat.label: Registered Jun 1995 → first trading day 2 Apr 1996

scenes.receipt: Incorporated Jun 1995 → Nasdaq IPO 2 Apr 1996 · Lycos SEC 10-Q (1996); Encyclopedia.com
scenes.voiceover: Lycos, an American search engine that began as a Carnegie Mellon University project. The company was incorporated in June nineteen ninety-five, and it went public in April nineteen ninety-six, just ten months later, then the youngest company ever to list on Nasdaq.

scenes.name: Lycos
scenes.headline: Sold to Terra Networks for $12.5 billion
scenes.receipt: Lycos SEC 10-Q (1996); Encyclopedia.com
scenes.voiceover: Four years later, in twenty hundred, Lycos was bought by Spain's Terra Networks in a twelve and a half billion dollar deal.

scenes.headline: Speed didn't predict survival
scenes.voiceover: Look at the pattern. Seven of the ten listed during America's nineteen nineties internet boom, and three during China's tech boom of twenty eighteen and nineteen. Some became giants. Others collapsed within a year or two. Going public fast told investors very little about who would survive.

scenes.headline: No South African company made this list
scenes.body: Three questions to ask about any hyped new listing: How old is it? What does it earn? Who is selling shares at the IPO?
scenes.voiceover: No South African company made this list. But if you ever hear hype about a brand-new listing, ask three questions. How old is the business? What does it actually earn? And who's selling their shares at the I P O? This is education, not financial advice.

scenes.headline: Which of these surprised you most?
scenes.voiceover: Which one surprised you most? Tell us in the comments. All our sources are in the description.

endcard.title: Speed isn't success
endcard.subtitle: Subscribe for South African money, explained.
